label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: blockers COMPLETE, other edges 4, samples with blocking 32

A.rule: a non-ledger_app session blocked ledger_app sessions in 32 samples

report.summary: Transfers show 7% HTTP 500s and multi-second tail latency. The only fault observed is an "other" session idle in transaction blocking ledger_app sessions at 06:52-06:54. The link to the 500s is not confirmed.

findings.claim: Transfers have 43 HTTP 500s (ratio 0.0708) and p95 1.54 s / p99 3.10 s latency.
findings.reason: Request metrics are complete and show the server errors and slow tail.

findings.claim: A non-app session (78272) idle in transaction blocked ledger_app sessions for up to 1.94 s between 06:52:08 and 06:54:06.
findings.reason: Session 75064 was blocked in 19 samples and 75809 in 8, both waiting on idle-in-transaction 78272.

findings.claim: Lock waits behind the idle transaction plausibly explain the slow and failed transfers, but no per-request timing or error text confirms it.
findings.reason: The blocking window overlaps the slow-request symptom, and pool exhaustion is excluded (0 timeouts, 0 pending), leaving lock waits.

findings.claim: Outbox delivery and consumer latency are healthy and do not explain the symptom.
findings.reason: 566 of 566 deliveries succeeded in about 71 ms, and arrivals match publications.

limitations: Blocking is sampled every 2 s and starts at 06:52:08, so it does not cover the earlier part of the window, and no request-level timing or 500 error text was collected.
The identity and owner of session 78272 are unknown, and whether the 43 errors fall in the blocking period is not shown.
next_checks: Correlate the timestamps of the 500s and slow transfers with the 06:52-06:54 blocking window, and pull the application error messages.
Identify session 78272 in pg_stat_activity (client, query, transaction start) and find why it holds a transaction open.

alternatives.reason: There were 0 acquisition timeouts and 0 pending borrowers, and the mean acquire time was 0.09 ms.
alternatives.hypothesis: Connection pool exhaustion caused the slow or failed transfers.

alternatives.reason: The failed count is constant at 1034 and predates the window, and all in-window deliveries succeeded.
alternatives.hypothesis: The outbox backlog (1034 FAILED, oldest undelivered age about 47,000 s) is related to the transfer errors.
